rows.title: Xi opens more pork access as Carney loosens steel restrictions during China visit
rows.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed in Shenzhen on Nov. 17, ahead of the APEC summit, to lift trade barriers on more goods. China will remove its extra 25% tariff on Canadian frozen pork cuts, frozen cold-water shrimp, Greenland halibut, some mollusks and sea cucumber, covering about $400 million of Canadian exports a year, under an arrangement that now runs to late 2028. In return, Ottawa extends tariff remission on certain Chinese steel and aluminum products and adds 32 more items (23 steel, 9 aluminum) that Canada does not make in sufficient supply. China will also open its market to Canadian fava beans, chickpeas and lentils, and both sides plan a 2027 trade mission and a 'year of e-commerce'. The deal is part of Canada's effort to diversify trade away from the United States, though canola oil still faces a Chinese duty and critics raise security and human-rights concerns.
rows.fact: China will drop its 25% tariff on about $400 million a year of Canadian pork and seafood exports, with relief running to late 2028. Canada extends steel and aluminum tariff remissions and adds 32 Chinese product categories. Canadian trade data suggest exports to China are up about 40% since the leaders' January meeting.
rows.outlook: Ottawa expects a pet food and wild aquatic products agreement by year-end and a major Canadian trade mission to China in 2027.
rows.why: 관세를 서로 낮추는 '맞교환'이 어떤 산업에 이익과 부담을 주는지, 그리고 미국 의존도가 높은 나라가 왜 교역 상대를 다변화하려 하는지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a tariff swap creates winners and losers across industries, and why a country that depends heavily on one trading partner tries to diversify its trade.
rows.term_def: A government decision to waive or refund a tariff on certain imports, often because domestic producers cannot supply those goods.
rows.note: Key figures ($400 million in relief, 32 added steel/aluminum items, relief to end-2028) cross-checked against a Reuters report (The Standard, Hong Kong) and Euronews. Distinct from the Nov. 10 Vancouver financial-services agreements covered on Nov. 13. The meeting was Nov. 17, so this is slightly older than 24 hours.

opinion.title: FIRST READING: What Carney's 'strategic partnership' with China will cost Canada
opinion.author: Tristin Hopper
opinion.summary: The columnist argues the new deal is lopsided: Canada's gains are food-market openings that Beijing could withdraw at any time, while China's gains, such as a foothold for its EVs and finance sector, are harder to reverse. Former detainee Michael Kovrig calls the arrangement asymmetric and recalls how China cut off Canadian canola in 2019 during a diplomatic dispute. The column warns that steel and aluminum remissions could become a loophole for mislabelled or transshipped Chinese metal. It puts the scale in context: Carney claims about $7.5 billion in new market access from his China outreach, while Canada sold $55.2 billion to the U.S. in September alone, so the China deal equals only a few days of U.S. exports. Auto industry and union leaders quoted in the piece doubt Chinese carmakers would build full plants in Canada.
opinion.why: 무역 다변화의 이익과 함께 '상대국이 언제든 철회할 수 있는' 비대칭 위험을 따져 보게 해 주어, 무역 협정을 비판적으로 평가하는 시각을 기를 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It weighs the benefits of trade diversification against the risk of one-sided deals a partner can revoke at will, helping readers judge trade agreements critically.

rows.title: Fed minutes: Higher interest rates needed in December as inflation worries mount
rows.summary: Minutes of the Federal Reserve's Oct. 27-28 meeting, released Nov. 18 (U.S. time), show nearly all officials expect to raise the benchmark rate by a quarter point in December, and two raised the idea of a half-point hike. The Fed held its key rate at about 3.9% (a 3.75%-4% range) in October after its first hike in three years in September, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. A large majority of officials worried that inflation could stay high even as gas prices fall and the effects of tariffs and the AI infrastructure build-out fade, and they noted price pressures are spreading beyond energy and tariff-hit industries. The minutes also flagged fast-growing, opaque debt tied to AI investment as a financial-stability risk. Higher rates have already pushed mortgage rates above 7% and weakened home sales.
rows.fact: Nearly all Fed officials expect a December rate hike, and two floated a half-point move. The Fed held rates at 3.75%-4% in October on a vote with two dissents in favour of hiking. Officials see inflation pressures broadening beyond energy and tariffs.
rows.outlook: Futures markets put the odds of a December hike near 95%, and some officials expect several more increases before spring 2027.
rows.why: 중앙은행이 물가를 잡기 위해 금리를 올리는 이유와, 그 결정이 주택담보대출 금리·집값 등 일상 경제로 어떻게 번지는지 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It explains why a central bank raises interest rates to fight inflation and how that choice spreads to mortgage rates, housing and everyday borrowing.
rows.term_def: A detailed written record of a central bank policy meeting, released a few weeks later, that shows what officials discussed and hints at future rate moves.
rows.note: Rate range, dissents and 'almost all' language cross-checked against Yahoo Finance's report on the minutes.

opinion.title: Fed minutes name the AI buildout as a reason more rate hikes are coming
opinion.author: Judith Murphy
opinion.summary: This analysis focuses on how the minutes treat the AI boom as part of the inflation problem rather than only a growth story. It notes officials said tariff effects are fading while AI-driven demand is pushing up prices of tech goods and spreading beyond data-center industries. Citing staff estimates, it puts September headline PCE inflation at 3.6% and core at 3.1%. It highlights the minutes' warning about rapid, opaque AI-related borrowing, including off-balance-sheet leases and circular financing among AI firms, and wider spreads on high-yield data-center bonds. The author argues that no official in the minutes treated the AI boom as a reason to stop raising rates, as stocks fell for a fifth straight session.
opinion.why: AI 투자 붐처럼 수요가 공급보다 빨리 늘면 물가가 오르고 금융 위험도 커질 수 있다는 점을 보여 주어, 기술 혁신과 거시경제의 연결을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how an investment boom like AI can push demand ahead of supply, raising inflation and financial risks, linking technology trends to macroeconomics.

rows.title: South Korea's exports top $1 trillion for first time on chip boom
rows.original_source: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources via The Korea Herald
rows.summary: South Korea's cumulative exports for 2026 passed $1 trillion at 2:09 p.m. on Nov. 19, the trade ministry said, making it the fourth country to reach the mark after Germany, the United States (both 2006) and China (2007), and the first new member in 19 years. The ministry projects full-year exports of about $1.17 trillion, up roughly 65% from the 2025 record of $709.3 billion. Semiconductors drove the surge: chip exports hit $396.8 billion in January-October, about 43% of the total and nearly triple the previous record for the period, thanks to AI data-center demand. Exports excluding chips still rose 20%, but imports grew 21%, leaving a January-October surplus of about $295 billion. Officials noted much of the growth is price-driven and that chips and petrochemicals create relatively few jobs, so the gains are concentrated in large firms.
rows.fact: Korea's exports crossed $1 trillion on Nov. 19, the fourth country ever to do so. Chips made up about 43% of January-October exports at $396.8 billion. The January-October trade surplus was about $295 billion.
rows.outlook: A trade official said exports could top $1 trillion again next year, but easing chip and oil prices could pull them below this year's level.
rows.why: 수출 '1조 달러'라는 성과가 반도체 가격 상승에 크게 기대고 있다는 점을 통해, 수출 호황이 왜 고용과 국민 생활 개선으로 고르게 이어지지 않을 수 있는지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows that a record export boom built largely on chip prices may not spread evenly into jobs and living standards, revealing the limits of export-led growth.
rows.term_def: The amount by which a country's exports are larger than its imports over a period.
rows.note: Milestone time, $1.17 trillion forecast and chip figures cross-checked with The Korea Times report on the same ministry announcement.

opinion.title: [Editorial] The trillion-dollar test
opinion.author: Korea Herald editorial board
opinion.summary: Written as exports neared the milestone, the editorial argues the $1 trillion mark exposes how dependent Korea is on chips. It notes semiconductors made up about 43% of exports and nearly three-quarters of export growth this year, while autos and petrochemicals are far smaller shares. It points to a widening gap: large firms' third-quarter exports more than doubled while small firms' rose about 10%, and over half of workers were in industries where real wages fell. It also warns that the U.S. trade surplus with Korea has more than doubled, inviting trade friction. The board urges using the windfall to revive broader manufacturing and build high-value services, rather than letting overseas factories replace production at home.
opinion.why: 한 산업에 대한 의존, 대기업과 중소기업의 격차, 무역흑자가 부르는 통상 마찰 등 수출 호황의 그늘을 함께 생각해 볼 수 있게 해 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It highlights the downside of an export boom: reliance on one industry, a gap between big and small firms, and trade friction caused by large surpluses.

rows.title: Eurozone inflation confirmed at 4 per cent in October
rows.summary: Eurostat's final estimate, published Nov. 18, confirmed that annual inflation in the euro area rose to 4.0% in October from 3.8% in September, its highest in about three years and double the European Central Bank's 2% target. Energy was the main driver: energy prices rose 21% from a year earlier, revised up from the flash estimate of 20.8% and up from 19% in September. Services inflation edged up to 3.3% and non-energy industrial goods to 1.2%, while food, alcohol and tobacco was revised down to 1.5%. Inflation varied widely by country, with Italy jumping to 5.6% from 4.2% and Lithuania, Bulgaria and Greece even higher. Because energy rather than broad demand is pushing prices up, the ECB faces a hard choice between fighting inflation and protecting a weak economy.
rows.fact: Euro area annual inflation was confirmed at 4.0% in October, up from 3.8% in September. Energy prices rose 21% year on year and services 3.3%. Italy's rate jumped to 5.6% from 4.2%.
rows.why: 에너지 가격 같은 '공급 충격'이 물가를 끌어올릴 때 금리 인상이 왜 어려운 선택이 되는지, 그리고 같은 통화를 쓰는 나라끼리도 물가가 왜 다른지 배울 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a supply shock such as soaring energy prices makes rate hikes a tough call, and why inflation differs so much among countries sharing one currency.
rows.term_def: Headline inflation counts all prices, including volatile energy and food; core inflation leaves those out to show the underlying price trend.
rows.note: Eurostat's own release page could not be loaded; the 4.0% figure, the 3.8% September rate and component data were cross-checked against Trading and Investment News and IndexBox reports on the same release. Different event from the UK inflation story covered on Nov. 18. Released Nov. 18 (about 27 hours before this edition).

opinion.title: Eurozone October inflation brings ECB closer to December hike
opinion.author: Carsten Brzeski
opinion.summary: ING's global head of macro, writing on the flash estimate of the same 4.0% October figure, says headline inflation is still being driven by the Middle East war and oil prices, while core inflation held at 2.5%, a sign that energy costs are not yet spreading widely. He expects winter heating demand and low gas storage to push gas prices higher and feed into retail prices early next year, so things should get worse before they improve. Unlike 2022, he argues, consumers are less able and willing to pay higher prices, so firms are more likely to absorb costs through thinner profit margins. For the ECB, he sees arguments on both sides: headline inflation above its forecast supports a hike, but subdued core inflation argues against aggressive tightening. His conclusion is that a December hike is now more likely and could be the last of the cycle.
opinion.why: 전문가가 헤드라인 물가와 근원 물가를 나눠 보며 금리 경로를 판단하는 과정을 보여 주어, 중앙은행 정책을 읽는 방법을 익힐 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows an economist separating headline and core inflation to judge the likely rate path, a practical lesson in reading central bank policy.

rows.title: BI raises rate to 6 percent to defend rupiah against Fed moves
rows.summary: Bank Indonesia raised its benchmark BI-Rate by 25 basis points to 6% on Nov. 18, lifting its deposit facility rate to 5.25% and lending facility rate to 6.75%, for a total increase of 125 basis points this year. Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti called the move pre-emptive, aimed at anchoring inflation within the 1.5%-3.5% target in 2026-2027 and guarding against further U.S. rate hikes in December and possibly 2027. The decision came after the rupiah hit a record low of about 18,285 per dollar, the weakest performance among emerging Asian currencies this year, amid foreign capital outflows and political uncertainty at home. Officials said higher rates alone are not enough, so the central bank is also intervening in currency markets and offering incentives that lower hedging costs to attract foreign investment. Inflation was 3.23% in October and growth 5.47% in the third quarter, so the hike is mainly about defending the currency rather than cooling an overheated economy.
rows.fact: Bank Indonesia raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 6%, its fourth hike since May and 125 basis points in total this year. The rupiah had fallen to a record low near 18,285 per dollar. The bank is also intervening in currency markets and offering hedging incentives.
rows.outlook: A senior deputy governor said the bank expects the Fed to hike once more before year-end and then pause in 2027, depending on data.
rows.why: 미국이 금리를 올리면 신흥국 통화가 약해지고 자본이 빠져나가는 이유, 그리고 신흥국 중앙은행이 성장보다 환율 방어를 택하는 상황을 이해할 수 있습니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why U.S. rate hikes weaken emerging-market currencies and pull capital out, and why some central banks raise rates to defend their currency rather than to cool growth.
rows.term_def: When investors move money out of a country, for example by selling its stocks and bonds, which tends to weaken its currency.
rows.note: Rate levels and the 125 bp cumulative figure cross-checked with Xinhua and an Investing.com report (Yahoo Finance), which also supplied the rupiah record low and the inflation and GDP figures. Announced Nov. 18 (about 28 hours before this edition).

opinion.title: Rupiah Rout Puts Bank Indonesia in a Monetary Policy Bind
opinion.author: Nasori
opinion.summary: Published on the eve of the decision, this analysis lays out the dilemma Bank Indonesia faced. The rupiah lost about 9% against the dollar this year, the second-worst emerging-market currency after Turkey's lira, as foreign investors pulled roughly $740 million out between mid-October and Nov. 10. Inflation rose partly because of food supply problems such as chili, fish and rice prices linked to El Nino, which interest rates cannot fix. Economists at the University of Indonesia's LPEM argued the bank should hold at 5.75%, saying a hike would not solve supply-side inflation and that recent bond inflows could ease pressure on the currency. The piece shows the bank ultimately chose the opposite path, putting currency stability ahead of these concerns.
opinion.why: 금리 인상이 환율 방어에는 도움이 되지만 공급 측 물가에는 효과가 작다는 반론을 소개해, 통화정책의 한계와 트레이드오프를 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It presents the case against hiking, that higher rates may defend a currency but do little against supply-driven inflation, illustrating the trade-offs and limits of monetary policy.
